summary.headline: Shemaroo Q2 FY27 revenue fell 2% YoY to ~INR 141 crore, but EBITDA loss narrowed to ~INR 2 crore from INR 55 crore.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was about INR 141 crore, down a marginal 2% YoY, while EBITDA loss narrowed sharply to about INR 2 crore from INR 55 crore a year earlier. Net loss reduced to about INR 8 crore from INR 45 crore, helped by completion of accelerated amortisation two quarters earlier and cost optimisation. Digital media grew 26% YoY to about INR 76 crore and was 54% of revenue, while traditional media fell 21% to about INR 66 crore, hit by the prolonged BARC rating blackout and deferred broadcaster content spends. Management reiterated that EBITDA break-even by year-end is an aspiration, not formal guidance.

segments.name: Digital media
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue ~INR 76 crore, up 26% YoY, driven by B2B licensing deals and YouTube ad revenue; about 54% of Q2 revenue and ~48% in H1. Management says licensing revenue is lumpy and should be judged over 12 months.

segments.name: Traditional media
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue ~INR 66 crore, down 21% YoY, due to BARC rating blackout reducing advertiser spend and broadcasters deferring content investments, which delayed TV licensing deals.

segments.name: Shemaroo Bhujrati (OTT)
segments.commentary: Released 9 new titles in the quarter across movies, web series and plays, including Lalo, Krishna Sada Sahayate, Zindagi Once More, Chaskaila S1, Shada Chani Bus, Stution and Ok Boss. Focus is on Gujarati and regional content.

segments.name: YouTube
segments.commentary: Flagship channel Shemaroo Filmi Gane passed 75 million subscribers; Shemaroo Entertainment channel crossed 62.3 million. Portfolio drew ~9.6 billion views in the quarter.

guidance_outlook: Management said it does not give formal guidance; the EBITDA break-even target by end of FY27 and cash-positive by FY28 are stated as aspirations.
Management expects EBITDA break-even at least by end of this year (FY27), moving further in FY28; the company says it remains very much working towards this.
Festive season is expected to support ad demand; management says demand is up YoY on both digital and traditional versus a weak festive season last year.
Net debt is directionally targeted to fall; management says net debt was held flat in Q2 and cash flow remains strong.
BARC rating blackout is a near-term challenge for traditional media revenues.
capex_capacity: Investment in new initiatives (television broadcasting and Shemaroo Bhujrati OTT) was ~INR 19.9 crore per an analyst question; management did not confirm the figure. Existing-operations EBITDA for H1 FY27 was stated as ~INR 35 crore before new-initiative spend.
Content spend is concentrated on digital, with rights bought as bundles for OTT, YouTube and licensing; TV channel budgets have been cut and programming rationalised.
Finance cost rose ~INR 0.45 crore on overall debt of ~INR 9 crore per management, due to temporary use of OD and CC limits to buy content. Company says it is not in debt.
demand_pricing: Traditional TV advertising is constrained because the absence of BARC ratings means advertisers cannot measure campaigns, so they price conservatively or shift spend to digital or print.
Festive-season demand is up YoY in both digital and traditional, versus a weaker festive season last year that was hit by GST cuts and logistics issues.
Licensing and syndication flow slowed in the geopolitical environment; digital revenue share dipped to about 40% in Q1 before rising to 54% in Q2, per management.
Management says YouTube continues to gain ad share versus other social platforms, citing Connected TV as a growth avenue.
Shemaroo is the worldwide digital and satellite distribution partner for the Telugu film Rambha Urvasi Menka.

qa_highlights.question: Is growth slowing in digital, given expectations of double-digit digital growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed geopolitical uncertainty hurting ad spend and slower licensing and syndication deal flow. Digital grew 3% in H1 but 26% in Q2 as delayed deals closed.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company stick to its guidance of EBITDA-positive FY27 and cash-positive FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it gives no guidance and these are aspirations; it is still working towards EBITDA break-even at least by end-FY27.

qa_highlights.question: How is the BARC rating blackout affecting the business?
qa_highlights.answer: No measurement means advertisers hesitate and price conservatively or move spend to digital or print. Broadcasters have cut content budgets, and the company has tempered its own channel budgets.

qa_highlights.question: What is the payback timeline on content?
qa_highlights.answer: TV licensing is upfront and fixed-fee on about five-year rights, so payback is short. Digital licensing covers 1-3 year rights, and YouTube and OTT are monthly variable revenue share.

qa_highlights.question: Why did finance costs rise in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Temporary use of OD and CC limits to fund content purchases raised finance cost by ~INR 0.45 crore on ~INR 9 crore of debt (as stated by management).

risks_watch: Traditional media revenue keeps declining (-21% YoY in Q2) while the BARC blackout continues with no measurement timeline.
Digital licensing revenue is lumpy, so quarterly results are hard to read; the 12-month view will be key.
Whether EBITDA break-even by end-FY27 is achieved; it is an aspiration, not formal guidance.
Digital growth slowed to 3% for H1, and the festive-season recovery needs to hold.
summary.management_tone: Cautiously optimistic: management highlighted EBITDA improvement and digital growth, while flagging the BARC blackout, geopolitical pressure on ad spend and lumpy licensing deals as near-term headwinds. Answers on guidance were carefully hedged, with the break-even target framed as an aspiration.
key_quotes: While overall operating revenue declined marginally by 2% year on year, we have continued to make meaningful progress on profitability with EBITDA improving by 96% compared to the corresponding quarter last year.
The prolonged bar rating blackout has impacted advertiser sentiment and grade on television advertising revenues.
Clarify we do not give any guidance. This is an ambition or aspiration that we have spoken about.

growth.why: Management explicitly says it gives no formal guidance; EBITDA break-even by end FY27 is an aspiration, not backed by disclosed capacity, orders or contracts, and Q2 revenue fell 2% YoY with traditional media down 21%.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA loss narrowed to ~INR 2 crore in Q2 FY27 from ~INR 55 crore, and H1 existing-operations EBITDA was ~INR 35 crore before ~INR 19.9 crore of new-initiative spend, but break-even by end-FY27 is an aspiration, not guidance.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No new plants, lines or capacity were discussed; content spend is being rationalised with TV channel budgets cut.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Digital grew 26% YoY to ~INR 76 crore in Q2 but only 3% in H1 (~INR 131 crore), while traditional fell 21% to ~INR 66 crore on the BARC blackout; festive demand is up YoY but licensing is lumpy.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: No capex plan was disclosed; content spend is concentrated on bundled digital rights and TV budgets were cut, and the company says it is not in debt with ~INR 9 crore of debt.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management gives no formal guidance, and Q2 revenue fell 2% YoY to ~INR 141 crore with traditional media down 21%.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: The EBITDA break-even by end-FY27 target is an aspiration, not formal guidance, and BARC blackout has no measurement timeline, with H1 EBITDA still ~INR -4 crore.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Nine new OTT titles were released in Q2 FY27 across Gujarati and regional content, and the company is focused on the Shemaroo Bhujrati pipeline.

rows.label: Digital licensing and syndication deal flow
rows.why: Digital grew 26% in Q2 as delayed B2B deals closed, but licensing is lumpy and H1 digital growth was only 3% (~INR 131 crore), so the 12-month view matters.

rows.label: Net debt directionally lower
rows.why: Net debt was held flat in Q2 with debt of ~INR 9 crore and management aspires to lower net debt, but the company is not formally committing to a figure.

rows.label: BARC ratings restoration
rows.why: Traditional TV advertising remains constrained with no measurement timeline, and traditional revenue fell 21% YoY to ~INR 66 crore in Q2.

tone.note: Management was confident on the EBITDA turnaround (loss down to ~INR 2 crore from ~INR 55 crore) and digital growth, but cautious on the BARC blackout, geopolitical ad pressure and lumpy licensing; analysts pressed on whether double-digit digital growth and FY27 EBITDA break-even are still achievabl
